rationale: In demonstration 1, colour 5 paints 4 downward and leftward, with the left ray stopping before colour 8. Demonstration 3 shows the same rays from colours 7, 6, and 3.
Colours 3 and 6 extend right in their own colours in demonstrations 1 and 2. In demonstration 3, colour 6 is blocked immediately by 8, while colour 4 extends to the right edge.
Colour 1 radiates in all eight directions. In demonstration 2 its downward ray preserves the 8 and continues below it; demonstration 3 radiates colour 3 while preserving encountered 9s.
Demonstration 1 has rays from colours 4, 5, and 6 in their own colours. In demonstration 2, colour 2's downward ray stops immediately before 8, while colour 4 radiates in all eight directions.
Colour 5 extends left to the edge in demonstration 1. In demonstration 2, its upper ray stops before 8, and colour 6's left ray stops before the existing 5.
Colours 3 and 1 fill their columns below with 4 in demonstration 1. Demonstration 2 fills the entire column through source 4, and demonstration 3 fills above and below sources 7 and 3.
Colour 6 paints upward with 4 in demonstration 1. In demonstration 3, that upward ray overwrites the encountered 8 with 4 and continues to the top; source 4 also paints upward.
Sources 4 and 2 paint rightward with 4 in demonstration 1. Demonstration 2 shows colour 3 stopping before 8; demonstration 3 shows colour 5 blocked immediately by 9.
Demonstration 1 extends colour 3 rightward over an 8. Demonstration 2 extends colours 5 and 6 to the right edge, overwriting encountered 9s with each source's own colour.
Sources 6 and 3 radiate 4 in all eight directions in demonstration 1. In demonstration 3, source 3's upward and leftward rays preserve encountered 8s and continue painting background beyond them.
